frequency_question: How often does the Department of Education proceed all the way to stripping a major accreditor of its federal recognition within a specific political term?
membership_rule: Includes any formal Department of Education review that advanced to the National Advisory Committee on Institutional Quality and Integrity (NACIQI) resulting in a de-recognition recommendation or formal limitation, excluding routine renewals without adverse action.

cases.name: Accrediting Council for Independent Colleges and Schools (ACICS) First De-recognition (2016)
ACICS Second De-recognition and Final Revocation (2022)

provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 3 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 3 named major de-recognitions in modern administrative history; tens of routine renewals excluded.
known_gaps: Excludes minor unrecognised bodies or voluntary relinquishments prior to formal departmental order.
skeleton: Formal administrative reviews of major, entrenched institutional or professional accreditors by the Department of Education where political friction is high.
multiplier: 3 confirmed terminal de-recognition actions against recognized accrediting agencies across approximately 30 major high-stakes review cycles over 30 years.
validity_reason: Tied directly to the current presidential administration's regulatory posture toward professional accreditation bodies.
